title: Kernels, cokernels, and exactness for discrete modules with continuous action
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group and $A$ a finite ring. Let $\mathcal C$ be the category whose objects are left $A$-modules with a $G$-action by $A$-linear automorphisms such that every element has open stabilizer, and whose morphisms are $A$-linear $G$-equivariant maps. The zero object and finite biproducts in $\mathcal C$ are the underlying $A$-module ones with componentwise action. For every morphism in $\mathcal C$, its kernel and cokernel in $\mathcal C$ are the underlying $A$-module kernel and cokernel with the induced action; these objects again have open stabilizers. A sequence in $\mathcal C$ is exact if and only if its underlying sequence of $A$-modules is exact. The abelian-category terminology is that of [def-sp-abelian].

source.place: Tag 0A2H, label section-group-cohomology: the continuity/open-stabilizer paragraph and the R-G-module discussion following Definition 04JP

proof.text: The zero module with its unique action is both initial and terminal. For two objects $M,N$, give $M\oplus N$ the action $g(m,n)=(gm,gn)$. The stabilizer of $(m,n)$ is the intersection of the two open stabilizers, hence open. The usual injections and projections are equivariant, and their componentwise universal properties among equivariant maps give a biproduct in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 04JP, label definition-G-module-continuous; zero object and finite biproduct verification

proof.text: For an equivariant $A$-linear map $f:M\to N$, the submodule $K=\{m\in M:f(m)=0\}$ is $G$-stable because $f(gm)=gf(m)=0$. Each $k\in K$ has the same stabilizer in $K$ as in $M$, so it is open. The inclusion $K\to M$ is equivariant. If an equivariant map $h:P\to M$ satisfies $fh=0$, its unique underlying module factorization through $K$ is equivariant since the inclusion is injective. Thus $K$ is the categorical kernel.

source.place: Tag 04JP, label definition-G-module-continuous; kernel calculation from the open-stabilizer condition

proof.text: The image $f(M)$ is $G$-stable, so $Q=N/f(M)$ has the induced $A$-linear $G$-action. For a class $[n]\in Q$, its stabilizer contains the open stabilizer of $n$; as a subgroup containing an open subgroup it is open. The quotient map $N\to Q$ is equivariant. Every equivariant $h:N\to P$ with $hf=0$ factors uniquely through it as an $A$-linear map, and the surjectivity of $N\to Q$ makes that factor equivariant. Thus $Q$ is the categorical cokernel.

source.place: Tag 04JP, label definition-G-module-continuous; cokernel calculation from the open-stabilizer condition

proof.text: Addition of equivariant maps is equivariant, giving a preadditive category. The kernel and cokernel calculations show that a morphism is monic exactly when its underlying map is injective, and epic exactly when its underlying map is surjective: if a cokernel is nonzero its quotient map detects failure of epicity, and dually for a nonzero kernel. An injective $f:M\to N$ identifies $M$ equivariantly with the kernel of $N\to N/f(M)$; a surjective $f$ identifies $N$ with the cokernel of $\ker(f)\to M$. Hence the criterion in [def-sp-abelian] makes $\mathcal C$ abelian. Finally the image of $M\xrightarrow{f}N$, computed as the kernel of $N\to N/f(M)$, is the module image with induced action. Thus $\operatorname{im}(f)=\ker(g)$ in $\mathcal C$ exactly when the underlying module sequence is exact at $N$; applying this at each term proves the claim for sequences.

source.place: Tag 04JP, label definition-G-module-continuous; direct category verification from the preceding calculations
